# Coverage-delta gate ack file (issue #415, incident #389).
#
# .github/scripts/coverage_delta.py fails a PR when a Playwright test title
# present at the merge-base is either absent at head or went from active to
# skipped, UNLESS this file carries a matching line. Same tether-discipline
# shape as docs_lint.py's in-file ALLOWLIST: mechanical check, human-written
# escape hatch, one line per exception, reason required.
#
# Format (append, never edit/remove someone else's line without checking
# with them first - these are a permanent record of a deliberate call, not
# a scratchpad):
#
#   coverage-ack: <test id or glob> — <reason>
#
# <test id> is `<path/to/File.spec.ts>::<full title>` (nested
# test.describe() titles joined with " > ", matching coverage_delta.py's
# own manifest key). A glob (`*`, `?`, `[...]`) is fine for "this whole
# file" or "this whole describe block" - e.g.:
#
#   coverage-ack: frontend/tests/Foo.spec.ts::* — reason
#   coverage-ack: frontend/tests/Foo.spec.ts::some describe > * — reason
#
# Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are ignored.

# Proposal H parked-spec port wave (2026-07-24, issue #272) - owner-ruled drops (file deleted,
# not just re-skipped). Full parity/upstreamability tables live in this wave's own PR body, not
# duplicated here - one line per exception, per this file's own convention above.

# rebuilt from scratch (container-first hero, Tokyo-11 tokens, owner rulings on BurstSvg/
# session-counter/WD3 phone compaction). Every ack below either (a) retires a test guarding a
# mechanism the rebuild deliberately deletes (sticky/bounded-height pinning, BurstSvg/HoverBurst,
# the gold/navy button treatment, the whatsthat-mark.svg glyph asset, the sliced-word pop
# animation) - not a coverage regression, since the underlying behavior no longer exists to test
# - or (b) covers a describe-block rename where the test's own assertions were kept/adapted, not
# dropped, under a new (still-covered, see the sibling test file) title. Full reasoning + the
# spec-section mapping live in PR #446's own body, not duplicated here.

# WTC phase C2 (issue #503, PR #551) - phase C1 was deliberately presentation-only, so this
# test asserted that tapping any candidate, grouped or ungrouped, submitted the IDENTICAL
# /2/submitPrintingTag/ payload. C2 intentionally supersedes that contract: a grouped tap now
# submits ONE illustrationId to the new /2/submitIllustrationVote/ endpoint instead, while an
# ungrouped tap stays on /2/submitPrintingTag/ unchanged. The old title now asserts the
# opposite of what's true, so it was renamed (not deleted) and split into two tests - one per
# branch - describing the new split; see the file's own "question feed - Level 2 illustration
# grouping" describe block for both replacements.
coverage-ack: frontend/tests/QuestionFeed.spec.ts::question feed - Level 2 illustration grouping > selecting a grouped candidate submits the identical payload to the identical endpoint as an ungrouped one — superseded by C2 (#503/PR #551): renamed + split into "selecting a grouped candidate submits its illustrationId to /2/submitIllustrationVote/, not a printing list" and "selecting an ungrouped candidate (distinct or null illustrationId) still submits to /2/submitPrintingTag/, unchanged" - the old title asserted C1's now-superseded sameness contract, not a coverage drop.

# Issue #301 (croppable bleed, merged bleed boxes, split-the-difference gutters) - layout.ts's
# fit math changed from "full bleed or drop a card" to "bare-card-count-first, bleed crops to
# whatever the space affords" (see layout.ts's own module comment / fitAxisWithBleed). The old
# title asserted the very behavior #301 was written to remove (a bordered profile dropping the
# sheet from 4x2 to 3x2 once bleed exceeded the cap) - that claim is now false, not merely
# renamed cosmetically, so the test was rewritten to assert the new (intended) outcome: the
# sheet stays a full 4x2, bleed on the affected edge crops to the cap instead. Same surface
# (Page Setup margin-profile control + live sheet slot count), same cap arithmetic
# (marginProfiles.test.ts's maxBleedForFourColumns is unchanged by #301 - only what exceeding
# it DOES changed), test still present and extended with a disclaimer-text assertion.
coverage-ack: frontend/tests/DisplayPage.spec.ts::DisplayPage (Proposal H, Step 1) > the margin-profile control defaults to Borderless (no warning) and switching to Bordered shrinks the sheet from 4x2 to 3x2, with a cap warning shown — renamed to "the margin-profile control defaults to Borderless (no warning) and switching to Bordered crops bleed rather than dropping to 3x2, with a cap warning shown (#301)" when #301 replaced the old "drop a column" behavior with per-edge bleed cropping; the sheet no longer shrinks to 3x2 at all under the new fit math, which is the fix this issue shipped, not a regression.
